sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

Challenging judgment and award dated 23.06.2018 passed by Principal Senior Civil Judge,
Hubballi, in MVC.no.390/2015, this appeal is filed by claimants for enhancement of compensation.
2. Though above matter is listed for admission, it is taken up for final disposal, with consent of learned counsel for parties.

3. Sri Chandrashekhar S Nagashetti, learned counsel for claimants at outset submitted that in claim petition filed by claimants seeking loss of dependency on account of death of Yallappa, tribunal after contest had held that accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of NWKRTC bus by its driver and claimants were entitled for compensation assessed by tribunal at Rs.9,06,000/- with interest at rate of 6% per annum.
It was submitted that only claimants were in appeal.
NWKRTC has not preferred appeal.
It was submitted that tribunal committed error insofar as assessing inadequate monthly income and failing to add future prospects.
4. On other hand, Smt. Veena Hegde, learned counsel for NWKRTC sought to support award.

5. Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment and award and record.
6.

From above submission and since only claimant is seeking enhancement of compensation, point that arises for consideration is:
"Whether claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for?"
7.
Insofar as monthly income, though claimants stated that deceased - Yallappa aged 42 years was working as agriculturist and earning Rs.25,000/- per month, same was not substantiated.
In absence, tribunal assessed his monthly income at Rs.6,000/- notionally.
B ut, notional income for year 2015 is Rs.8,000/-.
Therefore, same has to be considered.

2 8.
Admittedly, deceased was aged 42 years and self-employed, claim petition filed by his wife and three minor children i.e., '4' dependents.

Therefore, as per decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v/s Pranay Sethi and Ors., reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, multiplier applicable will be '14', addition of future prospects will have to be at '25%' and deduction towards personal expenses will have to be at '1/4'.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v/s Pranay Sethi and Ors., reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, loss of dependency would be as follows:
Rs.8,000/- + 25% -  X 12 X 14 = Rs.12,60,000/-.
9.

Apart from above, claimant no.1 would be entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards spousal consortium, claimants no.2 to 4 would be entitled to compensation of Rs.40,000/- each towards parental consortium.
They would also be entitled to Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and like sum towards loss of estate.

Since more than 3 years have lapsed after decision in Pranay Sethi's case (supra), 10% has to be added to compensation under conventional heads which would be:
Rs.40,000/- X 4 + Rs.15,000/- X 2 + 10% = Rs.2,09,000/-.

Therefore, total re-assessed compensation would be follows:
 Sl. Amount in  Conventional Heads  no. Rupees  1. Loss of dependency 12,60,000/-
 2. Loss of consortium  1,60,000/-
 (Rs.40,000/- X 4)
 3. Towards Funeral expenses 15,000/-
 4. Loss of estate 15,000/-
 5. 10% Addition 19,000/-
. Thus, point for consideration is answered partly in affirmative as above.

11. Consequently, following:
O R D E R i. Appeal is allowed in part.
ii. Claimants are held entitled for re-assessed compensation of Rs.14,69,000/- as against Rs.9,06,000/- awarded by tribunal with interest at 6% per annum from date of claim petition till deposit.
iii. NWKRTC is directed to deposit balance compensation within eight weeks.
iv. Directions issued by tribunal regarding apportionment, deposit and release shall be as per award of tribunal proportionately to enhanced compensation.
